channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: Chinese firm hires from A&O Shearman and HSF Kramer
item.description: Hui Zhong Law Firm has added to its international arbitration team in Hong Kong, hiring Kitty Zheng as a partner from A&O Shearman and Wu Hao as of counsel from Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer.

item.title: IBA panel explores “the electrification of everything”
item.description: A panel at the International Bar Association Arbitration Day in Abu Dhabi explored how the surge in demand for electricity is impacting the energy market and the types of disputes arising in the sector.

item.title: Telecom Italia fails to halt revival of US$15 billion claim
item.description: The French Court of Cassation has upheld the annulment of an ICC award that dismissed a Brazilian private equity group’s US$15 billion claim against Telecom Italia.

item.title: Bulgaria sees off Czech utility’s billion-euro ECT claim
item.description: Czech utility ČEZ has lost a billion-euro Energy Charter Treaty claim against Bulgaria over changes to the country’s electricity market – as the European Commission formally calls on 16 EU member states to withdraw from the treaty.

item.title: Hong Kong partner returns to Ashurst
item.description: Gareth Hughes has left Debevoise & Plimpton, where he headed the Asia litigation team, to rejoin the partnership at Ashurst in Hong Kong.

item.title: Hong Kong group may bring claim over Panama port concession
item.description: A Hong Kong-based conglomerate says it may bring international legal proceedings after the Panama Supreme Court cancelled a billion-dollar port concession that has emerged as a strategic project for both the US and China.

item.title: Bangladeshi state entity wins limited damages over gas field blowout
item.description: An ICSID tribunal has ordered a subsidiary of Canada’s Niko Resources to pay a small fraction of the US$800 million in compensation sought by Bangladesh’s national oil company over a blowout at a gas field two decades ago.

item.title: Wordstone hires former US investment arbitration chief
item.description: David Bigge has left his role as chief of investment arbitration at the US Department of State to help GAR 30 firm Wordstone Dispute Resolution launch a new office in Washington, DC.

item.title: Saudi power plant claims play out in Bahrain
item.description: A Saudi state-owned utility is facing three Bahrain-seated UNCITRAL arbitrations brought by contractors on a billion-dollar power plant project, with awards in two of the cases expected soon.

item.title: India defeats Korean utility’s treaty claim
item.description: An UNCITRAL tribunal has dismissed a US$400 million treaty claim brought against India by a subsidiary of a South Korean state-owned electric utility over an investment in a gas-based power plant.
